Webshell_PHP_Eval_Inflate.title: PHP webshell (eval/assert + gzinflate + base64 chain)
Webshell_PHP_Eval_Inflate.explanation: Conjunctive match of an executor (eval( or assert() with a decode primitive (gzinflate/base64_decode) is the canonical PHP obfuscated-webshell chain. v2.13.1 reclaims assert() as an alternative executor (the prior `not $assert` exclusion existed only to spare legit assert(decode(...)) unit-test code, which the context gate now demotes). Multi-string conjunction makes this a confirmed family indicator, not a single-token guess.
Webshell_PHP_Eval_Inflate.attacker: Operator with upload access planting a webshell
Webshell_PHP_Eval_Inflate.boundary: Web server process executes attacker PHP
Webshell_PHP_Eval_Inflate.asset: Host execution + data on the web server

Webshell_PHP_Exec_Passthru.title: PHP webshell (system/passthru/shell_exec/exec/popen exec chain)
Webshell_PHP_Exec_Passthru.explanation: Two command-execution primitives (system/passthru/shell_exec/proc_open/exec/popen) co-occurring with a request input binding ($_REQUEST/$_GET/$_POST) is the shape of a PHP command-execution webshell. v2.13.1 widens the exec set (exec(/popen() and the input set ($_POST); $_POST in PHP-tutorials/tests is absorbed by the context gate (prose-doc/test-fixture -> inferred).
Webshell_PHP_Exec_Passthru.attacker: Operator with upload access planting a webshell
Webshell_PHP_Exec_Passthru.boundary: Web server process executes attacker PHP
Webshell_PHP_Exec_Passthru.asset: Host execution + data on the web server

Webshell_JSP_Runtime_Exec.title: JSP webshell (Runtime.exec + request.getParameter chain)
Webshell_JSP_Runtime_Exec.explanation: Runtime.getRuntime().exec combined with request.getParameter is the canonical JSP command-execution webshell pattern.
Webshell_JSP_Runtime_Exec.attacker: Operator with upload access planting a webshell
Webshell_JSP_Runtime_Exec.asset: Host execution + data on the application server

Malware_Reverse_Shell_Stager.title: Reverse shell stager (socket + dup2 + shell spawn)
Malware_Reverse_Shell_Stager.explanation: socket.socket + dup2 + a shell binary (/bin/sh or cmd.exe) is the classic Python reverse-shell stager. The conjunction is a confirmed indicator, not a benign network client.
Malware_Reverse_Shell_Stager.boundary: Host process opens outbound socket to attacker
Malware_Reverse_Shell_Stager.asset: Interactive shell access on the host

Malware_Powershell_Encoded_Stager.title: PowerShell encoded-command stager
Malware_Powershell_Encoded_Stager.explanation: powershell with an encoded-command flag (-EncodedCommand or the short -enc/-ec/-e) paired with a stealth flag (-WindowStyle Hidden / -NoProfile or the shorthand -w hidden / -nop) is the standard dropper/stager invocation. v2.13.1 accepts the short-flag encodings and shorthand stealth flags real droppers use; PS droppers documented in prose/tutorials are demoted by the context gate. EncodedCommand hides the payload from plain-text inspection.
Malware_Powershell_Encoded_Stager.attacker: Malware operator invoking an obfuscated stager
Malware_Powershell_Encoded_Stager.asset: Host execution under the user context

Malware_HTA_Dropper.title: HTA dropper (mshta + WScript.Shell.Run)
Malware_HTA_Dropper.explanation: mshta paired with WScript.Shell and a Run/Shell.Application invocation is the shape of an HTA dropper executing a remote or local payload.
Malware_HTA_Dropper.attacker: Malware operator delivering an HTA dropper
Malware_HTA_Dropper.boundary: User-context script host executes attacker payload
Malware_HTA_Dropper.asset: Host execution under the user context

Cryptominer_XMRig_Stratum.title: XMRig / stratum cryptominer pool indicator
Cryptominer_XMRig_Stratum.explanation: A stratum pool URI (stratum+tcp:// or stratum+ssl://) co-occurring with an XMRig/cryptonight/randomx marker (incl. the quoted "rx/0" config form and common public Monero pool hosts: pool.supportxmr.com/xmrpool./nanopool./moneroocean/hashvault) is a confirmed cryptominer pool indicator. v2.13.1 widens the pool/algorithm marker set; mining-ops docs and pool lists in blocklists are demoted by the context gate.
Cryptominer_XMRig_Stratum.attacker: Malware operator hijacking CPU for mining
Cryptominer_XMRig_Stratum.boundary: Host process connects to a mining pool
Cryptominer_XMRig_Stratum.asset: CPU cycles + electricity on the host

Cryptominer_Coinhive_Browser.title: In-browser cryptominer (CoinHive / WASM wrapper)
Cryptominer_Coinhive_Browser.explanation: Two CoinHive/WASM-wrapper markers co-occurring indicate an in-browser cryptominer payload. Medium severity: browser-context, lower host impact than a native miner.
Cryptominer_Coinhive_Browser.attacker: Site operator hijacking visitor CPU for mining

Hacktool_Mimikatz.title: Mimikatz credential-dumper indicator
Hacktool_Mimikatz.explanation: Two Mimikatz markers (sekurlsa/logonpasswords/mimikatz/gentilkiwi) co-occurring indicate the Mimikatz credential-dumping tool. Medium: a hacktool presence, not an active exploit by itself.
Hacktool_Mimikatz.boundary: Operator process reads LSASS credential material

Hacktool_Metasploit.title: Metasploit framework indicator
Hacktool_Metasploit.explanation: Two Metasploit markers (metasploit/msfconsole/exploit-multi-handler/msfvenom) co-occurring, OR a meterpreter payload alongside msfvenom, indicate the Metasploit exploitation framework. v2.13.1 adds the meterpreter payload alternative. Medium: framework presence, not an active exploit.

Hacktool_LSASS_Dump.title: LSASS credential-dump indicator
Hacktool_LSASS_Dump.explanation: lsass.exe paired with a dump primitive (MiniDump/OpenProcess/comsvcs.dll/procdump) is the shape of an LSASS credential-dump. v2.13.1 adds procdump as a dump primitive. Medium: hacktool presence with credential-theft intent.
